# Cadence UI — full context

# Cadence UI

> Animation-first React components for shadcn. Base UI + Tailwind CSS v4 + Motion.
> Install with `npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/<id>`. Every component ships its motion contract and a reduced-motion branch.

## Install

```json
{ "registries": { "@cadence": "https://cadence.dev/r/{name}.json" } }
```

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

## Rules for agents

- Prefer an existing Cadence component over writing new animation code.
- Read the item's `docs` and `meta.motion` before changing motion.
- Keep the reduced-motion branch; never remove `data-motion`.
- Use presets from `components/cadence/lib/motion.ts`; do not invent durations.
- Cadence is UI only: never pass a schema, resolver, or validation rule to a component (P11).

## Components

- [Button](/r/button.md): Triggers an action, with press feedback that collapses under reduced motion. (form, feedback)
- [Dialog](/r/dialog.md): A modal window that fades and settles in, with the open and close sequence interruptible. (overlay)

## Docs

- [/r/registry.json](/r/registry.json): install index
- [/r/catalog.json](/r/catalog.json): machine-readable catalog
- [/llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt): every component doc inline


---

# Button

Triggers an action, with press feedback that collapses under reduced motion.

## When to use

- The primary action of a form, dialog, or toolbar.
- A single, clearly labelled command: save, delete, invite.
- Anywhere the user expects a physical press response.

## When not to use

- Navigation between routes; use a link styled with `buttonVariants`.
- Toggling a persistent state; use `toggle` or `switch`.
- Submitting a long-running job that needs its own progress surface; pair the button with a
  spinner and a `disabled` state, or use `toast` for the result.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";

export function Save() {
  return <Button onClick={save}>Save changes</Button>;
}
```

## Examples

### Variants

```tsx
<Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
<Button variant="destructive">Delete project</Button>
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Open settings">
  <Settings />
</Button>
```

### Links

For navigation, keep the link and take the styles: this preserves link semantics and
middle-click.

```tsx
import Link from "next/link";
import { buttonVariants } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";

<Link href="/pricing" className={buttonVariants({ variant: "outline" })}>
  Pricing
</Link>;
```

### Composition

`render` replaces the underlying element; use it for custom button components, not for links.

```tsx
<Button render={<CopyButton />}>Copy</Button>
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "destructive" \| "outline" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "link"` | `"default"` | Visual weight. |
| `size` | `"default" \| "xs" \| "sm" \| "lg" \| "icon" \| "icon-xs" \| "icon-sm" \| "icon-lg"` | `"default"` | Height and padding. |
| `render` | `ReactElement \| (props, state) => ReactElement` | – | Base UI composition; replaces `asChild`. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. |

All native button props are forwarded.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| press | `scale 1 → 0.98` while active | `spring.press` | yes (pointer up) |
| release | `scale 0.98 → 1` | `spring.press` | yes |
| reduced | no scale; colour and shadow only | – | – |
| none | no scale; colour and shadow only | – | – |

## Accessibility

- Renders a real `<button>` through Base UI, so Enter and Space activate it natively.
- Focus is visible through the ring tokens; disabled buttons are not focusable and keep
  `aria-disabled` semantics from Base UI.
- `aria-invalid` drives the destructive border and ring. The component does not validate
  anything: see [validation](/docs/validation).

## Notes for AI

- Keep the label specific ("Delete project", not "OK").
- Do not add a `loading` boolean that hides the label; pass `disabled` and render a spinner
  next to the text so the action stays readable.

# Dialog

A modal window that fades and settles in, with the open and close sequence interruptible.

## When to use

- A focused task that must interrupt the page: rename, invite, confirm.
- Content that needs a modal, a focus trap, and an obvious escape route.
- A short form whose result matters more than the page behind it.

## When not to use

- Non-blocking hints and menus; use `popover` or `tooltip`.
- Long multi-step flows; use a page or a wizard.
- Mobile sheets with drag gestures; use `drawer`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/dialog
```

This also installs `button`, which the dialog uses for its close control.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dialog/dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";

export function DeleteProject() {
  return (
    <Dialog>
      <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Delete project</DialogTrigger>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Delete this project?</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>This removes every deployment and cannot be undone.</DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <DialogFooter>
          <DialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
          <Button variant="destructive">Delete project</Button>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <DialogContent>…</DialogContent>
</Dialog>;
```

### Without the built-in close button

```tsx
<DialogContent showCloseButton={false}>…</DialogContent>
```

### Footer with a close action

```tsx
<DialogFooter showCloseButton>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</DialogFooter>
```

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI root. |
| `DialogTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the dialog. |
| `DialogContent` | `showCloseButton`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. |
| `DialogOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `DialogContent`. |
| `DialogClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the dialog. |
| `DialogHeader` / `DialogFooter` | `className` | Layout only. |
| `DialogTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `DialogDescription` | `className` | Optional supporting text. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | overlay `opacity 0 → 1`; panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.95 → 1` | `popup.anchored` | yes |
| exit | overlay `opacity → 0`; panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.95` | `exit.fade` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, 100ms | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | instant | – | – |

The panel stays mounted while its exit transition runs; Base UI delays unmount until the
transition ends, so reopening mid-exit reverses cleanly.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the dialog. |
| Escape | Closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. |

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`,
  focus trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling.
- The close button is a real button with a screen-reader-only label.
- `DialogTitle` is required; a dialog without an accessible name is invalid.
- Content is unmounted after the exit transition, so focus is never lost mid-flight.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is centred and capped at `max-w-lg`; on narrow viewports it keeps a 1rem gutter.
Long content scrolls inside the popup rather than the page.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open.
- Animates opacity and scale only; no layout reads and no JavaScript animation loop.

## Notes for AI

- Always render a `DialogTitle`; it is the accessible name.
- Keep the confirming action specific ("Delete project", not "OK").
- Do not animate height inside the dialog; mount content instead.
